items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I played with his band I played tenor banjo with him for a good while

ctx.x: Yeah Well he'd come along a little later, wouldn't he?

Well, no he was active in that time when Around the time that I'm telling you about now When Billy Phillips and all them places was running, you know Yeah The Hunts and Nagel When they was running, he was operating that was around 1912 He was playing then he had a good band Cause I played with his band I played tenor banjo with him for a good while Oh yeah Chris Kelly had He had all that work over the river He was playing over the river And of course, played white and colored dancers too But the majority of his…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Billy Phillips was on, uh, Saratoga near the next corner of, uh, uh, uh, uh, more near Benville.

ctx.x: They used to have your small band. Yeah.

Uh, well, you see, uh, they used to dance. They had, uh, they sell liquor there, you know, they had women working there, uh, hustling. And, uh, the fellas, people would come in there. Most of the men from off the ships, they'd come in there and spend money and dance. And go on and have a good time and put, uh, we had a kiddie box that we, that dropped the money in the kiddie box for the different numbers that they want to hear, you see. And, uh, now, uh, T-Net played, uh, the last I heard of him, he played with…

What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: Before you played with Billy Phillips Dancehall. Yeah, that was one. Yeah. And you were playing guitar in those days.

ctx.x: Did they have some of the blowing instruments too or mostly strings?

They had blowing instruments too, yeah. Oh, the dance band? Yeah, they had, I think Bunk Johnson was playing in one of the bands at that time. Remember Bunk Johnson? Bunk Johnson was playing with the Silver Leaf, I think. Well, I played with the Silver Leaf for a good while. There's spot jobs, you know, up on the Pelican. Who was the leader of that? Uh, uh, Poisey Umphrey. Oh, Percy or was it his father? No, Poisey. Poisey, yeah. Poisey Umphrey. Willie Umphrey. Willie Umphrey. Willie Umphrey, yeah. The clarinet…
Was that the place called, um, later the Entertainers or 101 Ranch? Yeah.
